reuse.why: Routes the four server copies of the midpoint rule and the new API field through the existing shared getScheduledAmount, but hard-codes the 7.5% tolerance instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: Removes four inline copies of the amount rule; the approximate tolerance formula is restated (Math.round(Math.abs(x) * 0.075)) rather than shared, and schedule-template's own midpoint copy is left in place.

placement.why: The expected-amount rule lives in shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount, used by the server, the API model and the client.

scope.why: Edits are limited to the amount rule, its callers, the API field and tests.

maintainability.why: The rule is mostly centralised, but the op is an optional stringly-typed parameter that the client callers do not pass (so they ignore the approximate rule), schedule-template.ts still computes a midpoint, and several comments still say 'furthest from zero' after step 4 changed the rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts re-implements the approximate tolerance instead of calling getApproxNumberThreshold (shared/rules.ts); server/budget/schedule-template.ts keeps its own isbetween midpoint instead of calling getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The tolerance formula is copied verbatim rather than disguised; the removed copies were replaced by helper calls.

abstraction_drift.where: amountOp parameter and an isapprox branch added to getScheduledAmount; server/budget/schedule-template.ts still computes the ranged amount itself (desktop-client callers call the helper without the op).
